name: Spiritual High
editorial_article: "Spiritual High (State of Independence)" is a defining electronic-pop production by the British collective Moodswings, featuring legendary vocalist Chrissie Hynde. Released in 1991, the track became a notable radio success, particularly for its atmospheric blending of ambient textures, downtempo electronic beats, and soul-inflected vocals. It serves as a reinterpretation—essentially a cover version—of the 1981 classic "State of Independence," originally composed by Vangelis and Jon Anderson. By integrating elements of trip-hop’s early blueprint with the haunting vocal delivery of The Pretenders' frontwoman, Moodswings created a bridge between late-80s sophisticated pop and the early-90s dance-ambient explosion. The song is perhaps most distinctively remembered for its inclusion of sampled audio from civil rights leader Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., which imbues the track with a layer of sociopolitical gravitas that was highly characteristic of the era's experimentation with multi-layered, soundscape-oriented production. Through the contributions of producers and engineers like those at Nice & Nasty, the track achieved a polished, expansive sound that transcended its dance-club origins, establishing it as a memorable artifact of early 90s British electronic production. Beyond its chart performance, "Spiritual High" remains a curious case study in how British acts of the period recontextualized 1970s and 80s prog-electronic foundations into the burgeoning downtempo and house scenes.
